stories.title: 20,000 Salmon Return to the Klamath River
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: After the largest dam removal project in U.S. history opened up the Klamath River last year, something wonderful has happened: about 20,000 chinook salmon have swum upstream to spawn in waters they haven't reached in over a century. The river runs through Oregon and California and was blocked for decades by four hydroelectric dams that cut salmon off from their historic spawning grounds. Local tribes fought for years to see these dams removed, and this massive salmon run is proof their work paid off. It's a rare and heartening example of a big environmental fix actually delivering results in real time.
stories.why_good: A concrete environmental restoration (dam removal) has already produced a measurable, joyful outcome for wildlife and the river ecosystem.

stories.title: Mexico Reintroduced Bison into Precious Desert Ecosystem After Century-Long Absence
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: Bison are roaming Mexico's Chihuahua Desert again after being gone for roughly 200 years. Conservationists carried out a series of reintroductions to bring the massive grazers back to this vital desert reserve. Bison act like natural gardeners, shaping the land and helping native plants thrive wherever they roam. Their return is seen as a major win for restoring the health of this fragile ecosystem for the long haul. It's a hopeful sign that lost wildlife can find its way home again.
stories.why_good: A real, completed conservation action that restores a keystone species and strengthens a fragile desert ecosystem.

stories.title: Nashville Singer-Songwriter Becomes Local Celebrity Rescuing Foxes and Saving Them from Mange
stories.label: animals
stories.summary: A country songwriter in Nashville named Jerry Vandiver has quietly become a local hero to the city's red foxes. Tennessee has been dealing with a bad outbreak of mange, a painful skin disease that can be deadly for foxes if left untreated. In his spare time, Jerry has been trapping sick foxes, treating them with medicine, and releasing them back to health. His gentle persistence has saved many animals and turned him into a beloved figure in his community. It's a lovely reminder of how much good one caring neighbor can do.
stories.why_good: A real, ongoing act of kindness that has genuinely helped sick wild animals recover, with no political angle at all.
